source.title: Generalization Bounds using Data-Dependent Fractal Dimensions
source.authors: Benjamin Dupuis; George Deligiannidis; Umut Simsekli

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The experiments measure whether a proposed data-dependent complexity measure tracks the training–test accuracy or loss gap, using correlations rather than the magnitude-aware perturbation measure in V7. The reported result bears on the broader question of measured properties tracking the gap, but does not test any listed version’s specific measure or behavior.
record.gate_note: The paper reports correlations between persistent-homology dimensions and generalization gaps, and compares the data-dependent dimension with the Euclidean-distance dimension. Results cited from other studies are not extracted. Figures 1–2 and 10–12 describe additional comparisons without numerical values in the text; their figure-only results are not separately extracted.
record.test_reason: The study tests whether fractal dimensions of SGD trajectories track generalization gaps. It does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness as specified in V7 or test any other listed version. Using Jiang et al.'s correlation statistics does not make this a test of Jiang et al.'s sharpness finding.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but omits the main theoretical contribution: generalization bounds using data-dependent fractal dimensions without a Lipschitz-loss assumption, with mutual-information terms and a geometric-stability condition for a further bound. Persistent homology enables numerical dimension estimation. Experiments generally improve correlations over Euclidean PH dimension, but do not evaluate the full bounds or show uniform improvement across every metric and setting.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures a data-dependent persistent-homology dimension along SGD trajectories and correlates it with generalization gaps; it does not test the claim versions’ interventions or named measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that higher learning rates and lower batch sizes seem to give less correlation in some settings; for CIFAR100, the reported relation depends on training accuracy/convergence. The paper notes correlation differs by dataset and network size.

fits_no_version.finding: Across the main experiments, data-dependent PH dimension correlates positively with generalization gaps and has higher aggregate correlation coefficients than Euclidean PH dimension. This advantage is not universal: Table 8's FCN-5 loss-gap correlations are slightly lower, and some batch-size-specific correlations in Tables 5 and 6 are lower. Larger-model experiments also show dependence on convergence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A data-dependent fractal dimension estimated from SGD trajectories can track generalization gaps, with predictive quality depending on the model, gap measure, hyperparameters, and convergence.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 202, 2023)
record.problems: The experimental correlations do not compute the full theoretical bounds because their mutual-information terms are difficult to estimate. The paper notes that loss functions used in experiments are not bounded in practice and that the bound's constant B is set to the maximum trajectory loss over experiments. Several additional comparisons are presented only as plots, and the authors note that correlation is lower in some learning-rate and batch-size settings.
record.rows_left_out: Figures 1–2, 4–12 include plot-based comparisons or extra model/dataset conditions without numerical values or textual coefficient values. Not extracted as rows because exact values cannot be assigned from the supplied text; the authors' qualitative figure descriptions are summarized in method_sensitivity and page excerpts.

untested.parts: No paired random-label and natural-label training and held-out evaluation.
No width sweep beyond the width needed to interpolate.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected test errors or intervention on local connectivity.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison; experiments use vanilla SGD.
Batch sizes vary, but the study does not report the required held-out-performance comparison under fixed epoch budgets; stopping depends on convergence or training accuracy.
No dropout intervention or comparison involving augmentation and removal of regularization.
No magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance, sharpness-gap correlation, or comparison of sharpness with norm and margin measures.
No removal of memorized examples and retraining comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The row values match the supplied tables. Their positive correlations are observed findings about a different construct; cannot_determine refers to their inability to establish a listed claim version. These are complexity-measure benchmarking rows and belong under fits_no_version. The reported ± quantities are standard deviations across seeds. No missing result bears on V1–V8.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps past interpolation and their effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers and their generalization.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and its interaction with augmentation and weight decay.
The study measures correlations with a data-dependent fractal dimension, not magnitude-aware sharpness or weight perturbation tolerance.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
